Tests that the (strict) eval scope is visible to the debugger.
--- Case 1: stack-allocated in eval ---
frame 0 scopes: eval,script,global
scope(0).a: 1
eval('a'): 1
eval('a++'): 2
--- Case 2: context-allocated in eval ---
frame 0 scopes: eval,script,global
scope(0).a: 1
eval('a'): 1
eval('a++'): 2
--- Case 3: inner function, stack-allocated in eval ---
frame 0 scopes: local,closure,script,global
frame 1 scopes: eval,script,global
eval('a'): Exception: ReferenceError
scope(0).a: <undefined>
--- Case 4: escaped inner function, stack-allocated in eval ---
frame 0 scopes: local,closure,script,global
frame 1 scopes: script,global
eval('a'): Exception: ReferenceError
scope(0).a: <undefined>
--- Case 5: inner function, context-allocated in eval ---
frame 0 scopes: local,closure,script,global
frame 1 scopes: eval,script,global
frame 1 scope(0).a: 1
frame 1 eval('a'): 1
frame 0 eval('a'): 1
frame 0 eval('a++'): 2
frame 1 eval('a++'): 3
--- Case 6: escaped inner function, context-allocated in eval ---
frame 0 scopes: local,closure,script,global
frame 1 scopes: script,global
frame 0 scope(1).a: 1
frame 0 eval('a'): 1
frame 0 eval('a++'): 2
--- Case 7: outer function called from inner function in eval ---
frame 1 scopes: local,closure,script,global
frame 1 eval('a'): 1
